checks: checkpoint P: an untouched copy of the checkpoint resumes (positive control)
checkpoint A: white space changed in both manifests, no value changed: accepted, identical result
checkpoint B1: a recorded value altered in manifest.json without updating its checksum: detected, the previous manifest used
checkpoint B2: the same alteration in both manifests: refused, nothing written or changed
checkpoint C1: the stored checksum of manifest.json altered, its data untouched: detected, the previous manifest used
checkpoint C2: the stored checksum altered in both manifests: refused, nothing written or changed
checkpoint D1: one byte of an engine state flipped: the state is discarded by its SHA-256 and the result is unchanged
checkpoint D2: an engine state truncated to half: the state is discarded by its length and SHA-256 and the result is unchanged
checkpoint E1: two committed generations, the newest manifest destroyed: the verified previous generation is used
checkpoint E2: a process killed during the first commit after such a recovery leaves the previous generation intact and resumable
checkpoint F1: the engine states named by the manifest removed: not treated as present, the seeds retrained
checkpoint F2: manifest.json removed: the previous manifest is used
checkpoint F3: both manifests removed, state files left: no checkpoint is assumed and no orphaned state is read
checkpoint S: the source checkpoint was not modified by any of these checks
memory E: control: with the automatic budget the same study completes and reports no memory stop
memory A: a 48 MiB process budget is reached: the study is stopped by it, incomplete and resumable, with a usable checkpoint
memory B: resumed with the automatic budget: saved work is kept, the study finishes with the measurements of the control
memory C: memory accounting in the result document and the checkpoint
memory D1: process budgets outside the supported range are refused and write nothing
memory D2: a budget below what the process needs before any training stops at once, keeps a valid checkpoint and resumes
controls N1: a successful resume (exit 0) is not accepted as a refusal
controls N2: an untouched resume is not accepted as a detection of damage
controls N3: a resume that needed the previous manifest is not accepted as an intact checkpoint
controls N4: a study that completed normally is not accepted as a memory stop

classes.1: implemented and independently tested (an independent implementation, an exact reference, or the unchanged 5.7 binary agrees)
classes.2: implemented and verified by the project's own tests on Linux, or by the Windows programs under Wine
classes.3: implemented, awaiting physical hardware validation (never executed on Windows hardware or an NVIDIA GPU)
classes.4: not implemented, unsuccessful, or not executed

controlWithThe57Programs.cause: The test gives the desktop host a private folder through HOME and USERPROFILE and then reads the saved study from that folder on disk. Under Wine the host did not use that folder: the study was found in the Wine profile (drive_c/users/root/Documents/EightMax/studies), and the folder the test reads stayed empty. A second run then also finds the study left by the first (the shared save folder that validation/5.6/wine/per-file.json describes for earlier releases). On Linux the same test passes with the 5.7.1 host, in the full regression run and with the AddressSanitizer build.
controlWithThe57Programs.classification: a limitation of running this test through Wine, present with the 5.7 programs too; not a regression of 5.7.1
